title: Coordinate Geometry
description: Comprehensive shared preparation notes and worked practice for Coordinate Geometry. Review the target examination syllabus and level before reuse.

sections.label: Concepts and worked examples
sections.html:
Cartesian plane

A point is written ((\(x,y\))): move horizontally by x and vertically by y. The origin is (\((0,0)\)); the axes divide the plane into four quadrants. Signs are (\(+,+\)), (\(-,+\)), (-,-), and (\(+,-\)) in quadrants I through IV.

Distance, midpoint and slope

For points (\((x_1,y_1)\)) and (\((x_2,y_2)\)), distance is (\(\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2+(y_2-y_1)^2}\)); midpoint is (\(((x_1+x_2)/2,(y_1+y_2)/2)\)). Slope is (\((y_2-y_1)/(x_2-x_1)\)) when (\(x_2 \neq x_1\)); a vertical line has undefined slope.

Lines

Slope-intercept form is (\(y=mx+c\)). Parallel nonvertical lines have equal slopes; perpendicular nonvertical lines have slopes whose product is (\(-1\)). The intercept form and point-slope form can be used when those values are known.

Worked example: Between (\((1,2)\)) and (\((4,6)\)), the slope is (\((6-2)/(4-1)=4/3\)), the midpoint is (\((5/2,4)\)), and the distance is (\(\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5\)).

sections.label: Methods and exam checks
sections.html:
• Keep x-coordinate changes and y-coordinate changes in consistent order.
  • Square both coordinate differences before adding in the distance formula.
  • For vertical lines, avoid dividing by a zero x-difference.
  • Sketch intercepts to check a line equation's signs and direction.
  • Use the midpoint to split a segment into equal parts.

sections.label: Key facts and formulas
sections.html:
• Distance formula comes from the Pythagorean theorem.
  • Midpoint coordinates are the averages of corresponding endpoint coordinates.
  • Horizontal line slope is 0; vertical line slope is undefined.
  • For (\(Ax+By+C=0\)), slope is (\(-A/B\)) when (\(B \neq 0\)).

sections.label: Worked practice
sections.html:
1. Core:

    Find the distance between (\(1,2\)) and (\(4,6\)).

    1. (\(4\))
    2. (\(5\))
    3. (\(6\))
    4. (\(7\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(5\))

    The coordinate differences are 3 and 4. Distance (\(=\\sqrt{3}^2+4^2}=\\sqrt{25}=5\)).

  2. Core:

    Find the midpoint of (\(-2,4\)) and (\(4,0\)).

    1. (\(1,2\))
    2. (\(2,1\))
    3. (\(-1,2\))
    4. (\(1,4\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(1,2\))

    Average the coordinates: (\(((-2+4)/2,(4+0)/2)=(1,2)\)).

  3. Foundation:

    In which quadrant is (\((-4,-2)\))?

    1. I
    2. II
    3. III
    4. IV
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: III

    Both coordinates are negative, so the point is in quadrant III.

  4. Standard:

    Find the midpoint of (\((2,-1)\)) and (\((8,5)\)).

    1. (\((3,2)\))
    2. (\((5,2)\))
    3. (\((5,3)\))
    4. (\((10,4)\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\((5,2)\))

    Average coordinates: (\(((2+8)/2,(-1+5)/2)=(5,2)\)).

  5. Challenge:

    What is the slope of a line perpendicular to a line of slope (\(2/3\))?

    1. (\(2/3\))
    2. (\(-2/3\))
    3. (\(3/2\))
    4. (\(-3/2\))
    Show answer and solution

    Answer: (\(-3/2\))

    Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals. The required slope is (\(-3/2\)), since (\((2/3)(-3/2)=-1\)).
